text:
Tyson Foerster played only 29 games for Philadelphia last season, scoring 13 goals in them, and this year has started slowly: 4 goals and 7 points in 22 games. The local coverage has noticed. The Inquirer argued the "slow start is par for the course," while the Delco Times wrote that the Flyers are "hoping Tyson Foerster is rounding back into form."

Our numbers lean toward patience. His expected goals, the quality of his chances, are 5.12, so he is a goal or so behind his chances, and he is scoring on 9.1% of his shots against a range that runs much higher. His shot is still one of the hardest around, in the 96th percentile for top speed.

The concern is more about his line. At five-on-five, Philadelphia has had only about 44% of the chance quality with him on the ice, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has him carrying the puck in on just 31% of his entries. One sign of trust: Charlie O'Connor of PHLY Sports reported on Nov. 16 that Rick Tocchet moved Foerster onto the power-play unit with Matvei Michkov and Trevor Zegras.
headline: Tyson Foerster's slow start has a story behind it
